description: AgriSense research synthesis (22-page PDF supplied by the owner): the selected EVIDENT invention, verdict states, assurance levels, gap planning, failure handling, re-evaluation, joint holdings, numeric table claims, proposed vs demonstrated capabilities, false premises, overlapping terminology, and unsupported performance claims. Answers restate the document; they are not independently verified facts. Separate from the core, VEIL, and structural benchmarks.

cases.question: What is EVIDENT, and what are the four mechanisms that form its core contribution?
cases.reference_answer: EVIDENT (Evidence-graded, Versioned Eligibility with Deterministic gap Targeting) is the selected core: an evidence-graded, version-aware eligibility engine. Its four mechanisms: assurance-typed evidence; assurance-aware multi-valued evaluation; minimum-cost gap targeting; bitemporal selective re-evaluation.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Owner's failing question 1 (2026-10-16: best score 0.325 < 0.35, model not called). The four parts are listed on page 12 (split across two chunks) and named on page 2; the expansion is on page 1.

cases.question: List all seven final verdict states supported by EVIDENT.
cases.reference_answer: ELIGIBLE_ESTABLISHED, ELIGIBLE_PROVISIONAL, CONTINGENT, INDETERMINATE, CONFLICTED, INELIGIBLE_ESTABLISHED, INELIGIBLE_PROVISIONAL.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Owner's failing question 2 (four passages passed, model declined). States listed on page 12; the final mapping on page 16.

cases.question: What does the minimum-cost evidence-gap planner calculate, and what costs does it consider?
cases.reference_answer: For a non-established verdict it computes the cheapest set of evidence acquisitions whose possible outcomes force a determinate verdict; each acquisition has a cost: farmer effort, fees, travel.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Owner's failing question 3.

cases.question: What are the main failure-handling rules when evidence is unavailable, a policy is ambiguous, verification fails or a co-holder withholds consent?
cases.reference_answer: Unavailable source: evidence stays at its current assurance and the decision is marked stale-risk. Ambiguous clause: the atom is INTERPRETATION_PENDING and dependent verdicts are at most PROVISIONAL. Proof failure: the A2-zk evidence is discarded and the system falls back to the lower level. Withheld consent: CONTINGENT, with the blocker named. Unknown is never converted to eligible.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Owner's failing question 4.

cases.question: What problem does EVIDENT solve?
cases.reference_answer: Eligibility facts come from heterogeneous evidence of very different reliability and the rules change through GRs and amendments, while existing systems collapse everything into a boolean eligible/not-eligible verdict and do not track which decisions a rule change invalidates.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Owner's question that already worked; check citations and the 'bit temporal' wording (garbled extraction in the old index).

cases.question: What are EVIDENT's assurance levels, from lowest to highest?
cases.reference_answer: A0 self-declared < A1 extracted from an unverified document (OCR) < A2 issuer-verified document < A3 authoritative registry response under consent.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Assurance lattice (page 15; also sketched on page 14).

cases.question: What happens to existing decisions when a new rule version is approved for a scheme?
cases.reference_answer: Only affected decisions (those whose decisive path or structure the change touches) are re-evaluated under the new version; the new decision is stored without overwriting the old one; if the verdict changes, the farmer is notified and attestations bound to the old decision are invalidated.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Rule-version propagation; pseudo-code on page 17.

cases.question: Which events trigger revalidation of decisions?
cases.reference_answer: Rule version changes, evidence expiry, a new 7/12 mutation (Ferfar), and consent withdrawal; they go through the dependency index and only verdict changes are notified.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Evidence-change propagation (workflow step 7).

cases.question: How is the eligible land area computed for a joint holding, and what happens when the shares are not recorded?
cases.reference_answer: Eligible area is the sum over the farmer's 7/12 entries of share fraction times parcel area; if shares are not recorded the atom is U (unknown), never an equal-split default (equal split only as a labelled what-if).
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Share arithmetic.

cases.question: When can a joint-holding application reach READY_TO_SUBMIT?
cases.reference_answer: Only when consent evidence from every listed co-holder is at the required assurance; eligible area is the farmer's own share.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Consent gating.

cases.question: What FY2026-27 allocation was announced for Bharat-VISTAAR, and how many central schemes does it cover?
cases.reference_answer: ₹150 crore; 10 central schemes.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Exact numbers from Part I.

cases.question: How many lenders did ULI have as of 12 December 2025, and what figure had Report 2 claimed?
cases.reference_answer: 64 lenders (41 banks and 23 NBFCs) per RBI's report; Report 2 claimed 89 lenders (found only on an exam-prep site).
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Table row: report claim vs. what was found.

cases.question: What rent does the MSKVY 2.0 scheme document specify, and what did Report 2 claim?
cases.reference_answer: INR 1,25,000 per hectare or 6% of the ready reckoner rate, whichever is higher, with 3% annual escalation (about ₹50,600/acre); Report 2 claimed ₹50,000/acre/yr +3%.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Table comparison with numbers.

cases.question: Which alternative architecture was selected as the core, and what happens to E's Aadhaar predicate?
cases.reference_answer: A (EVIDENT) is the core; E's Aadhaar predicate becomes one optional evidence type within A.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Selection decision (page 12).

cases.question: Which ideas from the two reports were rejected from the final design, and why was Report 2's Independent Claim 1 rejected?
cases.reference_answer: Rejected: dynamic zk-SNARKs, blockchain registries, in-circuit transliteration, ULPIN-keyed nullifiers, carbon/insurance arbitrage, satellite-determined survival entitlement, Report 2's bundled patent claim and 'world-first' positioning. Claim 1 (ZK + spatial + escrow) bundles three inventions.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Needs two distant pages (inventory table and decision register).

cases.question: Has EVIDENT been shown to reduce real-world benefit rejections for farmers?
cases.reference_answer: No. User-study outcomes, adoption and real-world rejection reduction are explicitly not claimed; they require a field pilot with consent and ethics approval. All performance statements are hypotheses to be measured.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Proposed vs. demonstrated: the answer must say it is not demonstrated.

cases.question: Since EVIDENT submits applications to MahaDBT automatically, how does it confirm that a sanction was granted?
cases.reference_answer: The premise is wrong: submission is manual, by the farmer or a CSC operator on MahaDBT; MahaDBT is the authoritative decision-maker and EVIDENT never claims sanction.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: False premise about automated submission.

cases.question: Why does EVIDENT treat unknown evidence as eligible so that farmers are not excluded?
cases.reference_answer: It does not: unknown is never converted to eligible; no path maps U or C to an eligible verdict (an invariant tested in the evaluator).
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: False premise contradicting the core invariant.

cases.question: What states does EVIDENT's application state machine move through?
cases.reference_answer: DRAFT -> EVIDENCE_PENDING -> CONSENT_PENDING -> READY_TO_SUBMIT -> SUBMITTED (manual) -> PRE_SANCTION_RECORDED -> FULFILMENT_DOCS -> CLOSED / REJECTED.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Overlapping terminology: application states vs. verdict states (page 12). Listing verdict states instead is wrong.

cases.question: What orchard survival thresholds apply to the Fundkar Falbag scheme?
cases.reference_answer: Sources conflict: some say 80% in year 1 and 90% in year 2, others 90% irrigated / 80% dryland; the report says to verify against the GR.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Conflicting secondary sources; the answer must not pick one.

cases.question: How does EVIDENT combine atom values with AND?
cases.reference_answer: F dominates; then C; then U; then F~; then T~; T only if all atoms are T.
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf

required_facts.description: T only if all atoms are T
match_any: only if all atoms are T

cases.notes: Formal composition rule.

cases.question: What is the complexity of exact gap planning, and what is used for larger rules?
cases.reference_answer: O(2^K · 2^M · |φ|) with K actions and M upgraded atoms; exact search is cheap for small per-scheme rules, and an ILP is used for larger rules (weighted set-cover variant, NP-hard).
expected_sources: AgriSense_ Research Synthesis, Selected Core Invention, and Roadmap.pdf
cases.notes: Numeric/formal detail of gap planning.

cases.question: What false-positive eligibility rate did EVIDENT achieve in its evaluation?
cases.notes: Unsupported performance claim: the false-positive rate is a planned metric (H1); no result is reported.

cases.question: What Anon Aadhaar proving latency was measured on the team's Android test devices?
cases.notes: Device measurements are planned (optional H5); the ~30 s figure is PSE's browser average, not a measurement on Android devices.

cases.question: How many farmers have used the EVIDENT engine so far?
cases.notes: No deployment or user study exists (the report says none is implied).

cases.notes: MahaVISTAAR-AI's reach is mentioned; no price is.
